newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed higher for the six successive trading day on Friday and ended at a new record, with financials, Unilever and high tech funds outperforming.
AEX share index rose one percent, or 6.99 points, to 719.49.
Royal Dutch was hurt by profit taking, after the stock gained 3.5 percent on Thursday when the oil firm released a strong increase in its 1996 results.
"It is just a reaction on yesterday's rise," said a dealer.
Unilever leaped and dealers said they noted strong interest from U.S. investors.

Unilever jumped 15.50 guilders to close at a new record of 351.00. "Especially U.S. investors turn towards Unilever as result of Tuesday's strong year-end results and the planned divestment of its chemicals business," said one dealer.

U.S. investors also blocked a further fall for Philips shares. "U.S. investors still like the stock because Boonstra (Philips chairman) said the 1996 dividend would be an unchanged 1.60 guilders this week and they liked the message," said one dealer.
He added that Dutch investors were less pleased by the announcement yesterday that Philips booked a net loss in 1996.
Dealers said the steady dollar, rising bond market, lower interest rates and new U.S. economic data were all taken well by the market.
U.S. January manufacturing output slipped 0.2 percent and the January PPI was down 0.3 percent.
"The Dutch market was already very positive and gained further after the U.S. data," said one dealer, adding a lower opening on Wall Street did not really harm Dutch stocks.
Another dealer said buying interest was mainly from small domestic investors and the U.S. and that some (Dutch) institutions started selling because the index is so high.
Financials were strong. ABN AMRO rose 3.50 guilders to a new record of 130.10 guilders and ING gained 0.80 guilders to 72.10.
Computer software firm Baan added 1.70 guilders to 95.40 guilders and dealers said the stock would surpass the 100-guilder level soon.

Retail and business services group Vendex, to publish its 1996/97 results on Tuesday, closed 2.10 guilders up at a new record of 89.30. The stock has been one of the favorites on the Amsterdam bourse since Vendex announced the acquisition of French Bis at the beginning of 1997.
